paper.title: Online Learning via Offline Greedy Algorithms: Applications in Market Design and Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Full-information adversarial online learning version of problem (1) with an extended (gamma,delta)-robust, Blackwell reducible offline iterative greedy algorithm
unmapped: general nonlinear reward functions f_t: D -> [0,1] from a function class closed under addition; offline problem admits a robust iterative greedy gamma-approximation
regret measured against gamma times best fixed point in hindsight (gamma-regret)
settings.definition_quote: In each round t, ADV picks a function f_t in F and simultaneously ALG takes an action by picking a feasible point z_t in C. ... full information feedback, where ALG observes the entire function f_t after choosing z_t

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit-information adversarial online learning version of problem (1) with an extended robust, bandit Blackwell reducible offline algorithm
unmapped: general nonlinear reward functions from a class closed under addition; offline problem admits a robust iterative greedy gamma-approximation
settings.definition_quote: bandit feedback, where ALG only observes the quantity f_t(z_t) after choosing z_t

settings.name_in_paper: Online sequential submodular maximization / product ranking (full information)
unmapped: reward is a sequential submodular function f(pi)=sum_i lambda_i f_i({pi_1..pi_i}) of a ranking of n items into n positions
settings.definition_quote: on every round t, a distribution over patience level lambda_t and the expected probability of click function f_t ... are chosen adversarially. ... After choosing the ranking, the platform observes the function f_t in the full-information setting.

settings.name_in_paper: Online sequential submodular maximization / product ranking (bandit)
unmapped: reward is a sequential submodular function of a ranking
settings.definition_quote: In the bandit setting, the platform only observes whether or not the consumer clicks on at least one item, but not which item was clicked on.

settings.name_in_paper: Maximizing Multiple Reserves (MMR) in second price auctions, full information
unmapped: action is a vector of personalized reserve prices for n bidders; reward is second-price auction revenue with adversarial valuation profile v_t in [0,1]^n
settings.definition_quote: each round t in [T] involves the seller choosing a set of reserves r_t and the adversary choosing a valuation profile v_t. In the online full information setting, the seller observes the valuation profile and gets credit for the resulting revenue.

settings.name_in_paper: Maximizing Multiple Reserves (MMR) in second price auctions, bandit
unmapped: action is a vector of personalized reserve prices; reward is second-price auction revenue
settings.definition_quote: In the online bandit setting, the seller observes just the resulting revenue and does not observe the bidders' valuations or even the identity of the winner.

settings.name_in_paper: Online non-monotone (discretized / continuous weak-DR) submodular maximization over [0,1]^n, full information
unmapped: reward functions are non-monotone continuous (weak-DR) submodular, restricted to a grid R^n or on [0,1]^n
settings.definition_quote: for continuous functions, our goal is to maximize a non-monotone continuous submodular function, either weak-DR or strong-DR, over the unit hypercube [0,1]^n

settings.name_in_paper: Online non-monotone (discretized / continuous weak-DR) submodular maximization over [0,1]^n, bandit
unmapped: reward functions are non-monotone continuous (weak-DR) submodular
settings.definition_quote: Furthermore, in the online bandit setting, there exists an online learning algorithm that obtains ... 1/2-regret.

settings.name_in_paper: Online unconstrained non-monotone set submodular maximization, full information
unmapped: non-monotone submodular set functions, unconstrained (all subsets of n items)
settings.definition_quote: For set functions, our goal is to maximize a non-monotone submodular set function without any constraints

settings.name_in_paper: Online unconstrained non-monotone set submodular maximization, bandit
settings.definition_quote: in the online bandit setting, there exists a learning algorithm that obtains O(nT^{2/3}) 1/2-regret

settings.name_in_paper: Online monotone submodular maximization with cardinality constraint k, full information
settings.definition_quote: consider the problem of maximizing a monotone submodular set function f:2^{[n]}->[0,1] subject to the cardinality constraint k

settings.name_in_paper: Online monotone submodular maximization with cardinality constraint k, bandit
settings.definition_quote: The greedy algorithm in [nemhauser1978analysis] satisfies (1-1/e,1)-robust approximation and is bandit Blackwell reducible.

settings.name_in_paper: Online maximization of monotone strong-DR submodular functions over a downward closed convex polytope, full information
unmapped: reward functions are monotone strong-DR submodular, L-Lipschitz smooth (f(x+v)-f(x) >= <grad f, v> - L/2||v||^2), gradient sup-norm bounded by U
learner observes gradients of f_t (full information)
settings.definition_quote: we consider an adversarial sequence of strong-DR submodular functions f_1,...,f_T, where for each t, f_t: P -> [0,1] for some downward closed polynomial-time separable convex polytope P with l2 diameter R_P. Moreover, f_t is L-Lipschitz smooth and ||grad f_t(z)||_inf <= U

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit Blackwell sequential game (vector-payoff approachability with costly exploration)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Vector-payoff Blackwell approachability game (multi-objective), objective is l_inf distance to a target set plus exploration cost, not a bandit regret.
unmapped: objective: l_inf distance of averaged vector payoff to target set S plus averaged exploration cost D(p) * #explore / T
player only receives an unbiased estimator of the vector payoff when paying an exploration cost
settings.definition_quote: A closed convex target set S is g(T)-bandit-approachable in the bandit Blackwell sequential game (X,Y,p,p_hat) if there exists a bandit player's strategy such that for every player 2's strategy, ... d_inf(1/T sum p(x_t,y_t), S) + E[1/T D(p) (#explore)] <= g(T)

algorithms.name: Online-IG (full-information online learning meta-algorithm with N parallel Blackwell algorithms)
Bandit-IG (bandit online learning meta-algorithm with N parallel bandit Blackwell algorithms AlgBB)
Online Frank-Wolfe with N parallel Blackwell algorithms (Algorithm 9)

symbols.D_p: l_inf diameter of the Blackwell vector payoff function
symbols.N_sub: number of subproblems of the offline greedy algorithm
symbols.delta_rob: robustness parameter delta of the extended (gamma,delta)-robust approximation
symbols.gamma: approximation factor of the offline algorithm

conditions: offline algorithm is an extended (gamma,delta)-robust approximation
tuning: Blackwell algorithm satisfying Theorem 1 (FTRL with l_q regularizer)

source.label: thm:full-info-online-meta
source.quote: Then, for this online problem, Online-IG runs in polynomial time and satisfies the following gamma-regret bound: gamma-regret(Online-IG) <= O(D(p) N delta sqrt(log(d_payoff) T))

results.notes: Gamma-regret against gamma*best fixed point. Example 1 gives O(k sqrt(log(n)T)) for monotone SM with cardinality constraint as a corollary (recorded separately).

symbols.D_p: l_inf diameter of the Blackwell vector payoff
symbols.D_phat: l_inf diameter of the unbiased payoff estimator

conditions: offline algorithm is bandit Blackwell reducible (exploration sampling device giving unbiased payoff estimates)
tuning: exploration probability q = D(p)^{-2/3} D(p_hat)^{2/3} (log d)^{1/3} T^{-1/3}

source.label: thm:banditILO
source.quote: Then, for this online problem, Bandit-IG runs in polynomial time and satisfies the following gamma-regret bound: gamma-regret <= O(D(p)^{1/3} D(p_hat)^{2/3} N delta (log(d_payoff))^{1/3} T^{2/3})

symbols.D_p: l_inf diameter of payoff (also the exploration cost)
symbols.D_phat: l_inf diameter of the unbiased payoff estimator

conditions: access to a separation oracle for S

source.label: thm:bandit-blackwell-thm
source.quote: A closed convex set S is O(D(p)^{1/3} D(p_hat)^{2/3} (log d)^{1/3} T^{-1/3})-bandit-approachable in the bandit Blackwell sequential game if and only if S is response-satisfiable

results.notes: Bound on distance to target set plus normalized exploration cost (time-averaged), not regret. Out-of-scope setting.

symbols.D_low: min{D(p), D(p)} as defined in the paper

conditions: hard instance: X = simplex over n actions, Y={0,1}^n, Bernoulli adversary

source.label: thm:bandit-blackwell-lower-bound
source.quote: there exists an adversary's strategy such that for every player 1's strategy, ... d_inf(1/T sum p(x_t,y_t), S) + E[1/T D(p) (#explore)] >= Omega(D_low T^{-1/3})

results.notes: Time-averaged approachability lower bound; out-of-scope setting.

source.label: thm:seqsub
source.quote: For the problem of maximizing sequential submodular functions in the online full information setting, there exists a learning algorithm that obtains O(n sqrt(T log n)) 1/2-regret

results.notes: Corollary cor:rank-general restates the same bound for product ranking (Asadpour et al. model).

source.label: thm:seqsub
source.quote: Furthermore, in the online bandit setting, there exists a learning algorithm that obtains O(n^{5/3}(log n)^{1/3} T^{2/3}) 1/2-regret

results.notes: Corollary cor:rank-general restates for product ranking.

conditions: benchmark 1/2 max over reserves in the finite grid R^n

source.label: thm:mmr
source.quote: for the problem of maximizing personalized reserve prices in the online full information setting, there exists a learning algorithm that obtains O(n T^{1/2} log^{1/2} m) 1/2-regret

conditions: benchmark 1/2 max over reserves in finite grid

source.label: thm:mmr
source.quote: Furthermore, in the online bandit setting, there exists a learning algorithm that obtains O(n m^{2/3} T^{2/3} log^{1/3} m) 1/2-regret

tuning: discretization of reserves chosen depending on T

source.label: cor:mmr
source.quote: there exists a learning algorithm that obtains O(n T^{1/2} log^{1/2} T) 1/2-regret ... Here, the benchmark in the regret bounds is 1/2 max_{r in [0,1]^n} sum_t f(r, v_t)

tuning: discretization depending on n and T

source.label: cor:mmr
source.quote: Furthermore, in the online bandit setting, there exists a learning algorithm that obtains O(n^{3/5}T^{4/5}log^{1/3}(nT)) 1/2-regret.

symbols.m_grid: number of potential values per coordinate

conditions: discretized submodular functions on R^n with |R|=m
max function value normalized to one

symbols.m_grid: number of potential values per coordinate

source.label: thm:usm

conditions: max function value normalized to one

source.quote: maximizing a coordinate-wise L-Lipschitz non-monotone (continuous) submodular function in the online full-information setting, there exists a learning algorithm that obtains O(n T^{1/2} log^{1/2}(LT)) 1/2-regret

results.notes: Learner needs L for discretization (not added to setting learner_knows).

source.quote: Furthermore, in the online bandit setting, there exists a learning algorithm that obtains O(n L^{2/5}T^{4/5} log^{1/3}(LT)) 1/2-regret
(1-1/e)-Regret(Algorithm 2) <= O(k sqrt(log(n)T)), which exactly matches the bound known in [streeter2009online]

results.notes: Stated in an example as a direct corollary of Theorem full-info-online-meta.

source.quote: (1-1/e)-regret(Algorithm 4) <= O(kn^{2/3}(log n)^{1/3}T^{2/3})

results.notes: Intro text says O(kn(log n)^{1/3}T^{2/3}); example and table say n^{2/3}. Recorded the example.

conditions: monotone strong-DR submodular, L-Lipschitz smooth (beta = L)
downward closed convex polytope with l2 diameter R_P

source.label: thm:DR-SM
source.quote: under full-information setting, Algorithm with N iterations obtains O(R_P U sqrt(Tn log n) + T L R_P^2/N) gamma_N-regret

results.notes: Paper's L is the smoothness constant, mapped to beta; R_P mapped to diam_K.

tuning: N = sqrt(T) L R_P / (U sqrt(n log n))

source.label: thm:DR-SM
source.quote: By setting N = sqrt(T) L R_P / (U sqrt(n log n)), we get O(R_P U sqrt(Tn log n)) gamma_N-regret.

results.notes: Corollary corr:strong-DR-SM-matroid gives O(R U sqrt(Tn log n)) on matroid polytopes with rank R (same form).
